lead: Uber ended its ride-hailing service in Nigeria after 12 years, and NNPC reported that its July profit nearly halved as oil and gas output fell. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike said he would be the first casualty if President Tinubu lost in 2027, while a House panel said it had traced 58 bank accounts to the head of a fake investment council. Diphtheria cases were confirmed in Nasarawa, and the Lassa fever death toll for the year reached 252.

items.h: Uber ends ride-hailing service in Nigeria after 12 years
items.s: Uber wound down its ride-hailing operations in Nigeria with effect from Wednesday, 2 September 2026, also leaving Uganda. The company arrived in Lagos in 2014 and later expanded to Abuja and other cities.

items.h: Wike says he would be the first target if Tinubu loses in 2027
items.s: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike said he would be the first casualty should President Tinubu lose the 2027 election to Atiku Abubakar or Peter Obi. Wike, still a PDP member, has made Tinubu's re-election central to his politics.

items.h: NNPC's July profit falls 48% to N279bn as output drops
items.s: NNPC Limited's monthly report showed profit after tax of N279 billion in July 2026, down from N535 billion in June, on revenue of N3.087 trillion. Crude oil and gas production fell during the month as disruptions hit operations.

items.h: SEC proposes up to N5bn minimum capital for forex trading platforms
items.s: The Securities and Exchange Commission published draft rules for online forex and contracts-for-difference trading, proposing minimum capital of N3 billion for brokers and N5 billion for trading platforms. The rules would bring local and offshore platforms under formal regulation.

items.h: House panel traces 58 bank accounts to head of fake investment council
items.s: A House of Representatives committee said the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council was never lawfully created and that the appointment letter of its director-general, Adeyemi Adeniyi, was fraudulent. Its interim report linked 58 accounts and 12 entities to him and cleared Femi Gbajabiamila.

items.h: Borno commissioner withdraws 'finger-breaking' threat as police step in
items.s: Saina Buba, Borno's commissioner for youth and sports, took back a remark made at an APC event in Maiduguri in which he threatened to cut off fingers pointed at officials. Police had already begun investigating the comment.

items.h: Atiku presses Tinubu over US drug case as FBI filing is cited
items.s: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar challenged President Tinubu to answer questions about American records rather than resort to personal attacks. A lobbying firm cited an FBI declaration filed on 28 August in a US court stating that Tinubu was a subject of an investigation in the early 1990s.

items.h: Police dismiss three officers over killing of UNIPORT graduate
items.s: Police dismissed three officers after the shooting of Anthony Obodo, a 22-year-old driver and University of Port Harcourt graduate, on 27 August. The killing triggered protests across Rivers State.

items.h: Troops kill terrorists and seize 793 rounds of ammunition in Zamfara and Kaduna
items.s: Operation Fansan Yamma said its soldiers killed several terrorists and recovered guns and 793 rounds of ammunition in separate raids in Zamfara and Kaduna on 2 September.

items.h: Fire damages part of Zamfara governor's residence in Gusau
items.s: Fire broke out at about 7.20pm on Tuesday in part of Governor Dauda Lawal's residence in the Government Reserved Area of Gusau, and firefighters were deployed.

items.h: Diphtheria outbreak confirmed in Nasarawa with 15 cases
items.s: The Nasarawa State Ministry of Health confirmed 15 diphtheria cases, most of them in Keffi Local Government Area, its director of public health said in Lafia.

items.h: Kano turns to traditional rulers to boost diphtheria vaccination
items.s: The Kano State Centre for Disease Control asked traditional rulers to mobilise communities for diphtheria vaccination after an outbreak in Rano Local Government Area.

items.h: Lassa fever deaths this year reach 252, NCDC says
items.s: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control recorded 14 new confirmed Lassa fever cases in week 33, in Ondo, Bauchi, Edo and Benue, bringing the year's total to 1,035 cases and 252 deaths.

items.h: OPay asks DSS and police to investigate shutdown rumour
items.s: Fintech company OPay said it is working with the Department of State Services and the police to trace false social media claims that it is closing its Nigerian operations.

items.h: Kwara Assembly declares seats of two defecting lawmakers vacant
items.s: The Kwara State House of Assembly declared vacant the seats of the members for Edu and Irepodun constituencies after they moved from the APC to the PDP. The decision followed a letter from the state APC chairman.

items.h: Edo governor and Obaseki mourn PDP leader Dan Orbih
items.s: Governor Monday Okpebholo and former governor Godwin Obaseki paid tribute to Chief Dan Osi Orbih, who chaired the governing council of Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma, calling him a bridge-builder.

items.h: APC to profile Tinubu support groups as group queries Sheriff's appointment
items.s: APC national chairman Nentawe Yilwatda said the party will profile groups backing President Tinubu to coordinate the 2027 campaign. A South West support group asked the party to review Ali Modu Sheriff's appointment as North-East coordinator.

items.h: Nabena says Bayelsa APC remains strong after Sylva's exit
items.s: Former APC deputy national publicity secretary Yekini Nabena said the party will still win in Bayelsa despite the defection of former governor Timipre Sylva.

items.h: Uba Sani says tax reforms have raised national revenue to N21.6trn
items.s: Kaduna Governor Uba Sani told the Joint Revenue Board's 160th meeting in Kaduna that national tax revenue has reached N21.6 trillion since the 2026 reforms. He praised Nigeria Revenue Service chairman Zacch Adedeji.

items.h: FIFA backs Nigeria's football reforms and plans normalisation committee
items.s: FIFA president Gianni Infantino said the body supports Nigeria's football reform drive, and a normalisation committee is to be set up this week after the NFF board resigned.

items.h: Private sector credit rises to N83.43trn
items.s: Central Bank data showed credit to the private sector grew by N2.39 trillion between May and July 2026 to N83.43 trillion, with the largest monthly rise in June.

items.h: Seplat plans $1bn in dividends and 500,000 barrels a day
items.s: Seplat Energy chief executive Effiong Okon said the company aims to pay $1 billion in dividends over the next four to five years and raise output to 500,000 barrels a day.

items.h: Dangote Cement courts London investors ahead of LSE listing
items.s: Dangote Cement will hold a capital markets day in London as it prepares for a proposed secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange.

items.h: UAE's ePointZero to buy 90% of Azura Power
items.s: UAE-based energy firm ePointZero agreed to acquire a 90 per cent stake in independent power producer Azura Power, marking its entry into African electricity generation.

items.h: Crude passes $95 a barrel as US-Iran hostilities resume
items.s: Oil prices rose above $95 a barrel for the first time in five weeks amid renewed fighting between the United States and Iran and fears over supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.h: Abuja hospital denies organ harvesting claim as police investigate
items.s: Wellington Clinics in Abuja denied involvement in illegal organ harvesting from a kidney donor, Abubakar Hassan, as police opened an investigation, ThisDay reported.

items.h: Police say controlling roaming cows in Abuja is not their job
items.s: Police spokesperson Ani Iniedu said managing cattle on FCT streets is outside the force's mandate, and that officers will act only when animals are involved in an offence.

items.h: NABTEB releases June/July results; 79,504 earn five credits
items.s: The National Business and Technical Examinations Board said 79,504 candidates in its June/July 2026 examinations obtained five credits or more, including English and Mathematics.

items.h: TRCN warns teachers against fake registration portals
items.s: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria warned teachers, school owners and applicants about online platforms using its name to defraud people seeking registration and qualifying examinations.

items.h: Customs sets 7 to 15 September screening for recruits
items.s: The Nigeria Customs Service said shortlisted recruitment candidates will be screened and documented at its command and staff college in Gwagwalada, Abuja, from 7 to 15 September.

items.h: Zulum hands over 42-room lodge for patients' relatives at UMTH
items.s: Borno Governor Babagana Zulum handed over a 42-room apartment at the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital for relatives and visitors of patients.

items.h: Kaduna gives land to three 1996 Olympic gold medallists
items.s: Governor Uba Sani allocated plots and named streets after Daniel Amokachi, Garba Lawal and Emmanuel Babayaro, fulfilling a 30-year-old promise to the Atlanta 1996 team.

items.h: Kaduna raises pay of traditional rulers
items.s: Governor Uba Sani approved higher remuneration for emirs, chiefs, and district and village heads in Kaduna State, local government association ALGON said.

items.h: New Delta police commissioner unveils intelligence-led crime strategy
items.s: Delta's new police commissioner, Samuel Erale, outlined plans to tackle kidnapping, cultism, armed robbery and cybercrime across the state.

items.h: Government restates push for cheaper CNG transport
items.s: Minister of State for Petroleum (Gas) Ekperikpe Ekpo said the government will keep expanding compressed natural gas as a cheaper, cleaner transport fuel.

items.h: Police launch app to report financial fraud
items.s: Inspector-General Olatunji Disu launched the Nigeria Police Force Vigilant App and a closed user group with MTN to improve operations and tackle fraud.

items.h: Appeal Court judge Abdullahi Bayero buried in Kano
items.s: Justice Abdullahi Mahmud Bayero of the Court of Appeal's Kaduna division, who died in Cairo, was buried in Kano after funeral prayers at the Emir's palace.

items.h: Wife of suspected terrorist surrenders with two children in Borno
items.s: A 45-year-old woman and her two children surrendered to soldiers of the 112 Task Force Battalion in Mafa after escaping a terrorist enclave, Daily Trust reported.

items.h: Miyetti Allah tells Tinubu to free its leader or lose its votes
items.s: A Miyetti Allah leader said members would not vote for the APC in 2027 unless the group's detained leader is released.

items.h: ADC sets up committee to reconcile members after primaries
items.s: The African Democratic Congress inaugurated a committee to engage aggrieved aspirants and candidates after its primaries for the 2027 elections.

items.h: Nasarawa governor says Tinubu is aware of the hardship
items.s: Governor Abdullahi Sule told an APC meeting in Lafia that President Tinubu knows Nigerians are struggling under the economic reforms.

items.h: Power minister presents Nigeria's reforms as a model for energy security
items.s: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said Nigeria's electricity reforms could guide other developing economies seeking secure energy.

items.h: Police arrest 12 suspects over kidnapping and other offences
items.s: Police said 12 people were arrested over offences including kidnapping, armed robbery, homicide and motorcycle theft, Premium Times reported.

items.h: Elumelu's stake in Seplat now worth about $1.28bn
items.s: Tony Elumelu's indirect holding in Seplat Energy, through Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings, is now valued at about $1.28 billion.

items.h: Pivot's debut N100bn commercial paper oversubscribed
items.s: Downstream energy firm Pivot Integrated Energy Services completed its first N100 billion commercial paper issue, which drew N100.08 billion in subscriptions.

items.h: National Intermediate Games to build school sports pathway, organisers say
items.s: Organisers of Eko 2026 said the games in Lagos from 1 to 15 October will help identify young athletes. About 15,000 are expected.

items.h: Researcher builds Igbo language data for AI
items.s: University of Chicago linguist Uduma Umeh is generating Igbo language data that could support the development of artificial intelligence tools.
